papers.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide strong representations for downstream classification tasks. Yet adapting a TSFM under changing operating conditions remains challenging. A model must improve on each newly observed condition without sacrificing conditions it has already learned, often from only a small labeled calibration set and without knowing the operating condition at inference time. We find that this difficulty has an important geometric structure. Under an operating-condition shift, the embedding space of a TSFM does not move uniformly: some local regions change substantially, while others remain nearly unchanged. Consequently, a global adaptation can unnecessarily move embeddings that were already correctly classified. To address this, we propose the novel PACT (Piecewise Adaptation via Chart Transport). PACT partitions the frozen source embedding space into local charts and learns lightweight residual transports for the regions affected by each new condition. An explicit identity path is always retained, and a learned gate softly selects among the identity and accumulated transports for each input. The pretrained TSFM encoder, classifier head, and previously learned transports remain fixed. With only 5% labeled calibration data per arriving condition and no condition identity at test time, PACT maintains an average macro-F1 above 0.95 across a four-condition bearing-fault stream. Under homogeneous tasks and label spaces, similar retention-adaptation behavior is observed across public benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Sachithx/PACT.

papers.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
papers.abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

papers.title: Compute Before You Digitize: ADC-less Mixed-Signal Processing for Scalable Cryogenic Qubit Readout
papers.abstract: We introduce DIRAC, an ADC-less in-cryostat qubit readout architecture that uses analog computing to redraw the analog-digital boundary. Directly operating on the front-end's analog output, passive complex mixers perform the equivalent of digital demodulation, ping-pong active-RC integrators average their outputs into down-sampled per-qubit traces, and a time-domain stage digitizes them, eliminating Nyquist-rate ADCs. A TX-RX co-design derives the mixers' local oscillators from the readout transmitter's baseband rather than per-tone PLLs. A per-line calibration flow trains the matched filter jointly with the neural network, improving fidelity and enabling low-bit-width, low-voltage digital processing. Designed in 22 nm FD-SOI and evaluated at 4 K on 1.12M experimental shots, DIRAC matches the fidelity of a floating-point (FP32) digital pipeline for readout windows down to 750 ns, at 31.6$\times$ and 238$\times$ lower energy than the fixed-point (FxP) and FP32 pipelines. It cuts the total 4 K power per physical qubit by 50.4% and 68.6% relative to FxP and room-temperature flex cables, respectively. At a fixed logical-qubit count and 4 K budget, this yields, against FxP, a code distance larger by 2 to 6 and a 1.6-7.3$\times$ (Willow) and 4.9-204$\times$ (SI1000, $p = 10^{-3}$) lower logical error rate.

papers.title: EEG2MCU: Sensing-to-Execution Co-Design for Wearable EEG Inference
papers.abstract: Wearable EEG inference is constrained not only by model size, but also by the channel-dependent sensing front end that must process high-dimensional inputs before compact downstream computation. We present EEG2MCU, a sensing-to-execution co-design framework that treats electrode count as a hardware design variable through task-aware montage selection. EEG2MCU retains a compact time-frequency representation and generates only the INT8 regions required by each first-layer tile, avoiding full input materialization. Halo reuse and access-aware placement across Flash, SRAM, and tightly coupled memory further reduce redundant generation and data movement. On a Cortex-M7 MCU, EEG2MCU reduces peak SRAM by 11.38x relative to the baseline, including a 1.71x reduction from the 62-to-19 electrode montage, while reducing latency by 2.57x and energy by 2.48x. It retains 94-96% of full-montage accuracy, demonstrating practical high-dimensional EEG inference under tight embedded-resource constraints.

papers.title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering
papers.abstract: Images often require both denoising and interpolation, yet treating the two tasks separately is suboptimal: interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates subsequent denoising, while denoising may remove image details useful for interpolation. In this paper, we study joint image denoising and interpolation from a mixed graph filtering perspective, where denoising is modeled using undirected graph filters and interpolation using directed graph filters. We first establish that, under mild conditions, any (pseudo-)linear denoiser and interpolator can be interpreted as solution filters of maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problems regularized by undirected and directed graph smoothness priors, respectively. Guided by these results, we formulate graph-based joint denoising and interpolation problems using both directed and undirected graph structures. We characterize when joint denoising/interpolation reduces to a separable pipeline and when a genuinely coupled optimization is required. For the non-separable case, we recover sparse graph operators from given denoisers and interpolators, yielding an efficient linear-system formulation solvable via conjugate gradient. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed joint framework consistently outperforms separate denoising and interpolation pipelines across multiple denoiser-interpolator combinations.

papers.title: Synthesizing hyperspectral Data using generative Models to train spectral Unmixing Methods for low-cost Crop Residue Cover Mapping
papers.abstract: The spectral range of the Field Imaging Nanosatellite for Crop residue Hyperspectral Mapping (FINCH), developed by the University of Toronto Aerospace Team's Space System Division, poses significant challenges for hyperspectral unmixing to determine crop residue cover fractional abundances. The severe lack of standard indices necessitates the use of complex, data-driven unmixing models. Complex unmixing models require dense, well-distributed manifolds, whereas ground-truth datasets are sparse and expensive. To better leverage the information content in existing ground-truth datasets, this study presents a framework that decouples interpolation and abundance-mapping estimation via an intermediary conditional data generator, contrasting with traditional single-model unmixing pipelines. This decoupling enables the inclusion of physical prior knowledge about spectra, which is not natively accessible to unmixing models, thereby artificially expanding the dataset to serve as a Monte Carlo approximation of the population risk. To test this hypothesis, we have proposed two generator models: a 1D Conditional U-Net with Conformer Layers (GD-Streamline) and a Dual-Path Transformer Conditional Variational AutoEncoder (TCVAE), and two unmixing models: Multi-Layered Perceptrons (MLP) and Fourier Neural Operators (FNO). The results of the study indicate a need for rigorous integration and introduction of spectral priors within the scope of the proposed decoupling framework to prevent domain and mode collapse and hallucination by the generator models; otherwise, this leads to falsely approximated data manifolds, ultimately resulting in unsatisfactory and out-of-distribution unmixing performance.

papers.title: TinyMyo: a Tiny Foundation Model for Flexible EMG Signal Processing at the Edge
papers.abstract: Objective: Surface electromyography (EMG) is widely used in biomechanics, rehabilitation, prosthetic control, and human-machine interfaces. Generalization across subjects, recording systems, and acquisition protocols remains challenging. Existing EMG foundation models (FMs) have limited support for multiple downstream tasks and deployment on low-power devices. Methods: We introduce TinyMyo, a 3.6-million-parameter Transformer encoder pre-trained on public EMG datasets using self-supervised masked reconstruction. TinyMyo supports multiple tasks with minimal changes to the task-specific prediction head. Results: We evaluated TinyMyo on hand gesture classification, hand kinematic regression, speech production, and speech recognition. For gesture classification, TinyMyo outperformed previously reported EMG FMs, achieving accuracies of 87.98% on NinaPro DB5, 97.1% on UCI-EMG, and 96.6% on EPN-612. On the GAP9 ultra-low-power microcontroller, TinyMyo achieved an inference time of 0.785 s and consumed 44.91 mJ per inference at an average power of 57.18 mW. A 1.9-million-parameter variant processed 5 s and 1 s input windows in 0.496 s and 0.089 s, respectively. Conclusion: TinyMyo demonstrates that a compact, self-supervised EMG encoder can support multiple downstream tasks and run on a low-power microcontroller. Significance: To our knowledge, this is the first deployment of an EMG FM on an ultra-low-power microcontroller, opening a path to on-device motor intent decoding, neuromuscular assessment, and human-machine interaction.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Environment-Aware Beam Management for Massive MIMO: A Geometry-Driven Virtual Base Station Framework
papers.abstract: High-frequency massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems promise ultra-high data rates. However, efficient beam management remains challenging due to the prohibitive beam training overhead and intricate coordination required in multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) scenarios. To address these bottlenecks, environment-aware communications have emerged as a promising paradigm, leveraging site-specific knowledge to circumvent exhaustive pilot-based beam training and streamline multi-user communications. In this paper, we propose a geometry-driven framework that utilizes multi-modal environmental data, specifically regional 3D light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds and location information, to construct an offline virtual base station (VBS) database. By modeling dominant reflection paths via mirror symmetry across building facades reconstructed from the point clouds, the VBS database provides a compact and sparse description of the wireless propagation environment. Given a user location, the VBS representation supports online coarse channel reconstruction and the generation of a beamspace prior. To refine the coarse estimates, we design a VBS-assisted orthogonal-pilot (VOP)-based partial beam training scheme with limited online measurements. Finally, to coordinate beam selection under inter-user interference, we develop a hierarchical dual-agent dueling double deep Q-network for coordinated beam selection (DD3QN-CBS). Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves effective spectral efficiency over the evaluated stochastic, heuristic, and conventional learning-based baselines, while achieving competitive performance with fewer online beam measurements.

papers.title: Brownian Bridge Diffusion-Assisted Joint Channel Estimation and Data Detection for Jamming-Resilient OFDM Receivers
papers.abstract: In next-generation wireless networks, the growing density of devices and limited spectrum resources pose severe jamming challenges to fragile legitimate communication links in the wireless electromagnetic environment. Crucially, when jamming overlaps with pilot and data symbols in both time and frequency domains, it inflicts a severe bottleneck on receiver-side joint estimation and detection. Existing schemes often lack an effective framework to combat such jamming contamination, thereby failing to guarantee reliable transmission. To address this issue, we propose a Brownian bridge diffusion-assisted joint channel estimation and data detection (BBD-JCED) framework for jamming-resilient orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) receivers. The proposed framework consists of a jamming suppression module and a Brownian bridge-joint recovery module. The former identifies jamming-contaminated bins in the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain and suppresses the dominant jamming components through spectral notching. The latter establishes a Brownian bridge-based probabilistic graph to model the probabilistic transition process from the suppressed OFDM observation to the coded bits, and performs a reverse recovery process to enable enhanced joint channel estimation and data detection. Moreover, we derive a variational lower bound (VLB) to reformulate the intractable bit estimate problem into a tractable training objective, providing a probabilistic foundation for the loss function design. Furthermore, we develop a two-stage training algorithm to separately optimize the jamming suppression and Brownian bridge-joint recovery modules. Simulation results under representative jamming types demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior jamming suppression and bit recovery performance over the considered baseline schemes while maintaining competitive inference complexity.

papers.title: The Geometry of Mode Sampling in Reconfigurable MIMO Channel Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Pattern-reconfigurable arrays acquire channels by distributing radiation modes across their antenna elements. Equal mode counts fix the observation budget while leaving a spatial sampling choice that directly affects reconstruction of unmeasured channels. We establish how this assignment enters the inverse problem through the receive aperture and the coupling between propagation paths. For an isolated path with calibrated positive real responses, the power-weighted variance of antenna positions completely characterizes the assignment dependence of the profiled angle information at fixed mode counts. We then construct layouts with identical weighted apertures and different path correlations, exposing a limitation of aperture-based design in multipath propagation. A paired simulation study evaluates balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling using a common estimator with per-detection joint angle refinement. Balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error relative to ascending contiguous blocks when some modes are entirely unobserved, with improvements across nearly all tested scenes at high signal-to-noise ratio. When every mode is sampled, the mean benefit is more sensitive to rare large errors. Together, the analysis and experiments connect the spatial distribution of mode measurements to both extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Channel Model and Sensing Performance for ISAC: The Case of a Single Cylindrical Scatterer
papers.abstract: We propose an electromagnetic wireless channel model for accurate target localization in radar-like sensing scenarios. The model employs a self-consistent method grounded in wave scattering theory and imposing boundary conditions, providing the (impedance) channel transfer matrix for a propagation channel with a single target modeled as a cylindrical scatterer. The model is: 1) physics-based, as it includes electromagnetic interactions between objects; 2) unified, as it is valid in both near- and far-field regions. Within the canonical two-dimensional and 2.5-dimensional configurations with line-source and dipole-source excitations, respectively, the model supports dielectric cylinders with frequency-dependent permittivity. Localization accuracy is assessed via the Cramer-Rao lower bound for a dielectric cylinder with variable position, radius, and dielectric constant. Provisions for future extensions to extended targets are discussed in the context of 3GPP channel modeling.

papers.title: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting
papers.abstract: Quantum state tomography and shadow-based estimation rely on measuring Pauli observables. An experiment does not measure them one at a time: it chooses a measurement setting that assigns one of the bases X, Y or Z to each qubit, and a single run in that setting yields estimates of every Pauli observable compatible with it. We say that the setting covers those observables. We determine how many random settings cover a prescribed fraction of all Pauli observables. As the number of settings grows exponentially with the number of qubits, the covered fraction has a sharp threshold at a growth rate of $3^{3/4}$ per qubit, set by the rate-distortion function of covering at zero distortion. We give an explicit expression for the number of settings needed to reach a target fraction, accurate up to a remainder that reduces to a small oscillation for many qubits, and show that random sampling is asymptotically optimal up to a factor of less than 1.69. Coverage does not determine what a setting contributes to an estimator. Observables covered by one setting are estimated from the same outcomes, so their estimates are correlated. We quantify this correlation through the design effect of a setting, which equals the squared Pauli expectation that the setting captures and depends on the target state. We derive its mean over settings in closed form for every state and show that it can be estimated without bias from the measurement data. In simulations on six qubits, measuring settings needs 7.6 to 38 times fewer circuit runs than measuring the same number of observables independently. At high coverage, fitting the outcome histograms instead of averaged estimates roughly halves the reconstruction error, mainly because the fit counts how many settings cover each observable. The correlation itself costs such a fit about a factor of two, and a larger design effect signals more to gain from modeling it.

papers.title: DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays. By integrating linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging, we recast classical methods - including Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC - into a single structure. We extend this framework to accommodate ESPRIT-type methods by treating the number of simultaneously predicted subarray channels as an additional dimension. Furthermore, we adapt this approach to non-Gaussian signals, establishing a parallel framework for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. As a practical application, we propose universal, J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that estimate spatial super- resolution spectra within a unified computational architecture. This architecture produces spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods and any intermediate variations.

papers.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
papers.abstract: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances. Existing complete-ranging protocols for network localization require every node pair to exchange signals, which prolongs the ranging cycle. In this paper, we propose sparse signal-multiplexing network ranging (S-SM-NR), a task-oriented framework that adapts the transmit-listen schedule to the ranging task required by network localization. First, we establish the S-SM-NR framework by formulating the joint design of the task graph and the transmit-listen schedule. Then, we analyze the minimum round count required by S-SM-NR and establish a connectivity condition for network localization. Subsequently, we develop a closed-form joint design that constructs the sparse task graph and the balanced transmit-listen schedule. In particular, the joint design can achieve the minimum round count under the complete physical connectivity. Finally, simulations show that the proposed S-SM-NR scheme reduces the occupied-round count and improves the localization accuracy by shortening the ranging cycle.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Tri-Hybrid Multi-User MIMO Precoding: The Blessing of EM-Reconfigurable Antennas
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic (EM)-reconfigurable antennas provide multiple candidate radiation patterns per element, thereby introducing an additional EM-domain degree of freedom. Integrating radiation-pattern reconfigurability, realized as EM-domain precoding, with conventional hybrid analog--digital precoding yields tri-hybrid multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) precoding, which can substantially improve the spectral efficiency of wideband multi-user MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. However, the joint design of EM, analog, and digital precoding remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a tri-hybrid precoding network (Tri-PNet) based on Conformer, an emerging neural architecture that combines the local modeling strength of convolutional neural networks with the global dependency modeling of Transformers. Furthermore, two representative radiation-pattern modes, i.e., the non-regular mode and the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Technical Report (TR) 38.901 mode, are investigated. Tri-PNet is trained in an unsupervised manner to jointly learn EM, analog, and digital precoding by maximizing the average sum spectral efficiency. Its radiation-pattern selection network (RPSNet) employs a Conformer encoder to capture both local and global frequency-domain correlations, whereas its hybrid analog--digital precoding network (HPNet) combines cross-attention and dual-path processing with singular-value-decomposition (SVD) and zero-forcing (ZF) priors. Simulation results under both radiation-pattern modes demonstrate that Tri-PNet outperforms random EM precoding and conventional hybrid MIMO without EM precoding, approaches the greedy EM precoding search scheme with substantially lower online complexity, and remains robust to imperfect channel state information (CSI).

papers.title: Physical Layer Security for Digital Semantic Communication: A Bit-Level Perspective
papers.abstract: Digital semantic communication requires reliable recovery of task-relevant information at a legitimate receiver while limiting source reconstruction by an eavesdropper. Uniform bit protection, however, does not account for the heterogeneous reliability and secrecy requirements of semantic bits. This paper proposes a bit-level physical layer security (PLS) framework that learns these requirements and incorporates them into physical-layer resource allocation. We first introduce a wiretap semantic feature channel whose two-stage training learns per-bit target bit-flip probabilities for the legitimate receiver (Bob) and the eavesdropper (Eve). These targets characterize the reliability requirements at Bob and the secrecy protection requirements against Eve. Based on the learned targets, we formulate a joint power and artificial-noise (AN) allocation problem for a multiple-input single-output wiretap channel under a worst-case angular-separation model. For a given target profile, the optimal information-AN power split admits a closed-form solution, and the per-bit power allocation is obtained by water-filling. We further develop a leakage-aware selection method among multiple learned-target profiles and extend the design to multiple-input multiple-output channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a better trade-off between preserving reconstruction quality at Bob and degrading that at Eve than uniform power allocation and the evaluated learning-based secure semantic communication schemes.

papers.title: Modal Parameter Extraction via Propeller-Driven Vibration Testing
papers.abstract: Ground Vibration Testing (GVT) supports aircraft certification but often requires lengthy and costly campaigns. Propeller-driven Vibration Testing (PVT) is assessed here as an output-only alternative, in line with Operational Modal Analysis approaches such as Taxi Vibration Testing and Flight Vibration Testing. A cantilever Aluminium 7075-T6 wing spar is instrumented with seven accelerometers and excited by an outboard electric motor and propeller. Seven runs are carried out: a motor-off baseline, five constant-throttle cases, and a manual up-down throttle sweep. The acquired spectra indicate that the dominant resonances remain observable under propeller excitation, while low-throttle conditions introduce narrowband harmonics that may mask structural peaks; the sweep reduces persistent overlap. Modal parameters are identified for the baseline and sweep cases using the Natural Excitation Technique with the Loewner Framework (NExT-LF). The first two modes remain closely matched (Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC) > 0.99), whereas the third mode shows reduced repeatability (MAC = 0.827) and a larger frequency shift, consistent with propeller-induced bending--torsion coupling and non-ideal sweep control. Overall, PVT provides a viable complement to GVT for extracting low-frequency modal information and motivates pursuing future work on automated throttle scheduling and coupling-aware test planning.

papers.title: How to Receive Focused Beams in Near-Field MIMO? Analytical Combiners and Array Size Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper investigates receive combining for near-field beamfocusing in line-of-sight channels with antenna array misalignment. We propose and evaluate two analytical combiners: analog ANF-AC and digital ANF-DC. Beyond focusing the beam toward the transmitter, ANF-AC benefits from the proposed phase-flip corrections (PFCs), while ANF-DC additionally exploits Dirichlet-kernel-based amplitude tapering. ANF-AC closely matches theoretically optimal analog equal-gain combining (EGC), with an SNR gap below 0.006 dB. Similarly, ANF-DC matches optimal digital maximum-ratio combining (MRC). We then leverage the analytical properties of these combiners for link-level evaluation and optimization, deriving a closed-form expression for the optimal transmitter-receiver array-size trade-off that maximizes received SNR with analog combining. We also show that the optimized analog receiver performs within 0.84 dB of its fully digital MRC-equivalent counterpart. These results demonstrate that optimized analog combining (with potentially lower implementation complexity and cost, particularly at higher frequencies) can get close to the fully digital performance. Beyond the theoretical insights presented, the analytical tractability and EGC-like / MRC-like performance of our combiners enable accurate network-level mathematical studies of beamfocusing, such as coverage, capacity, and interference analysis and optimization toward efficient 6G+ near-field MIMO communication systems.

papers.title: Foundation Model-Driven Agentic AI for 6G
papers.abstract: Mobile networks are outgrowing manual tuning: parameters multiply, services diversify, and traffic shifts faster than experts can react. The machine learning (ML) models that automate radio control are narrow: each is trained for one task, degrades when conditions move, and needs specialist retraining. This article introduces FM-in-the-loop, a framework for 6G radio access networks in which a foundation model (FM) reasons while lightweight machine learning agents act. It reads operator intents in plain language, decomposes them into subtasks, coordinates task-specific agents over Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces, and supervises them across their lifecycle---while the orchestration FM never enters the latency-critical control path. We locate seven integration points across four lifecycle stages, compare three cloud-to-edge deployments, and evaluate two elements: channel representations from a wireless FM are tested under noise-level and channel-estimation-error shift, and an instrumented emulation of the orchestration loop reports the measured cost of turning an operator intent into dispatched agent goals. Hallucination, cost, and standardization barriers remain.

papers.title: Beyond RSRP: An Exploration of Alternative Metrics for Beam Management in an Urban Micro 5G NR Scenario
authors: Daniel J. Jakubisin (Hume Center for National Security and Technology
papers.abstract: Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) is widely used for beam selection in 5G NR as it is an easy indicator of path loss, but is not interference-aware, limiting its effectiveness in dense deployments. In this paper, we explore RSRP, Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ), and Signal to Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) as beam selection metrics alongside three UE-gNB association strategies in a 3GPP-compliant Urban Micro multi-cell simulation, benchmarked against Regularized Zero-Forcing (RZF) full-Channel State Information (CSI) upper bounds. Using a 3GPP-compliant Urban Micro multi-cell simulation benchmarked against RZF full-CSI upper bounds, we demonstrate two findings: directional RSRQ, despite its inter-cell interference awareness, is the worst-performing strategy in symmetric interference, and sequential association outperforms power-optimal Hungarian assignment. We also establish that the residual performance gap to full-CSI precoding stems from codebook quantization rather than metric imperfection, identifying adaptive codebook design as a mechanism to enhance performance.

papers.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Full Waveform Inversion for Attenuation Reconstruction in Ultrasound Computed Tomography
papers.abstract: Acoustic attenuation is more challenging to reconstruct and has received less attention than sound speed in ultrasound computed tomography using full-waveform inversion (FWI). In this study, a deep-learning (DL)-assisted FWI framework was proposed for attenuation reconstruction based on our previous work. Some numerical experiments were conducted to investigate the strategy and the effectiveness of using DL to help accelerate and improve the reconstruction quality of attenuation imaging in FWI. The results indicated that DL saved computational cost by 28% and improved attenuation reconstruction accuracy by 70% when combined with sufficiently accurate sound speed estimates. The result supports the potential of DL initialization to improve the computational efficiency and reconstruction quality of joint SOS and attenuation FWI.

papers.title: Fisher Information Characterization in GNSS DPE under Multipath-Induced Channel Uncertainty
papers.abstract: The availability and utilization of Fisher information in global navigation satellite system (GNSS) direct position estimation (DPE) under multipath-induced channel uncertainty are investigated. First, a unified estimation-theoretic framework is developed to characterize information mapping and utilization across direct and two-step receivers. Next, a scalar-equivalent statistical channel model for short-delay multipath is established via least-squares (LS) projection. Based on this model, receiver-state Cram\'er-Rao bounds (CRBs) are derived under perfect and statistical channel knowledge, while misspecified CRBs (MCRBs) are derived under a simplified deterministic complex-gain model that neglects channel uncertainty. The closed-form approximations and asymptotic analyses of the derived bounds further reveal how channel uncertainty affects different components of waveform-domain Fisher information. Our results reveal that: 1) DPE and fully coupled two-step estimation achieve comparable accuracy, whereas the performance loss caused by sequential decoupling substantially exceeds the additional loss from suboptimal weighting; 2) under statistical channel knowledge, improving received signal quality does not necessarily yield noticeable positioning gains; 3) positioning information remains available even as the coherent channel mean vanishes; and 4) neglecting channel randomness causes the MCRBs to diverge in this limit and can introduce positioning error floors that become more pronounced with longer observations.

papers.title: Towards Environment-Aware 6G Network Planning: An Any-to-Any Channel Knowledge Map Approach
papers.abstract: Planning sixth-generation (6G) networks for reliable coverage across diverse environments is challenging, as it requires channel knowledge between candidate network node locations and potential service regions. This article proposes an environment-aware network planning framework based on any-to-any (X2X) channel knowledge maps (CKMs), which characterize channels between arbitrary transmitter-receiver location pairs. Within this framework, we first construct X2X CKMs from environmental information, sparse channel measurements, or both, with map types and spatial resolutions selected according to the planning task. We then use these maps to predict coverage and optimize network deployment and configuration subject to service requirements and practical constraints, while accounting for subsequent network operation. Finally, field measurements assess channel prediction accuracy and deployment performance, providing feedback for CKM correction and deployment refinement. We discuss implementation methods and tradeoffs across these stages. Case studies illustrate the effectiveness of the framework for indoor intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) deployment and outdoor base station (BS) deployment. Live-network trials further demonstrate coverage gains from IRS deployment and BS reconfiguration, with measurement feedback supporting CKM calibration and configuration refinement.

papers.title: Trade-off Between Airspace and Channel Capacity for Low-altitude Wireless Network
papers.abstract: Communication-serviceable capacity for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks depends on both spatial occupancy and wireless quality of service (QoS). This paper formulates a communication-feasible occupancy-planning model that maps candidate-grid assignments to concurrent beam loads and per-user rates under fixed-stream and fixed-beam power. With fixed effective noise, per-beam QoS screening determines maximum admission, and an exact dynamic program maximizes aggregate spectral efficiency at that fixed admission. Signal-level simulations validate the SINR expressions, while an explicit-array model examines load-dependent inter-beam leakage. The dynamic program is globally optimal for the separable integer problem, but that guarantee does not extend to the coupled problem. Equal-time orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and ideal-SIC non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are evaluated through the same local beam reduction under fixed effective noise and fixed per-beam power.

papers.title: Multidimensional Source-Space MEG Representation of Network Imbalance in ADHD
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with an atypical imbalance between the default mode network (DMN) and task-control systems. However, compressing neural activity into a single macroscopic imbalance measure may obscure individual neurophysiological differences. To address this, we leveraged the source-orientation selectivity and related measurement properties of resting-state magnetoencephalography (MEG) to establish a multidimensional source-space network representation in 21 individuals with ADHD and 21 healthy controls. We defined the macroscopic imbalance in relative Alpha activity between the DMN and task-control systems as the Core, and expanded its constituent information along three dimensions: spatial sources, spectral composition, and temporal network organization: into in-depth measures, assessed for stability, robustness, and complementarity. We found that the ADHD group exhibited a significant Core Alpha imbalance, driven mainly by task-control regions, while the multidimensional expansion revealed complementary ADHD-related neurophysiological information not fully represented by the Core, suggesting that similar macroscopic imbalances may reflect distinct underlying physiological states. Across 40 exploratory within-cohort held-out evaluations with separate development and test subsets, mean ROC-AUC increased from 0.7607 (Core-only) to 0.8995 with multidimensional inputs and to 0.9051 with the final ensemble, and mean accuracy increased from 71.43% to 79.82%. These findings suggest that multidimensional source-space expansion can further clarify the neurophysiological composition of ADHD-related network imbalance and improve individual-level discrimination, offering an interpretable framework potentially applicable to other brain disorders characterized by network imbalance.

papers.title: Convolution-Augmented Transformer for Robust Blind CFO Estimation in LEO Satellite Communication System
papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communications are essential for achieving ubiquitous global connectivity. However, the high mobility of LEO satellites induces massive Doppler shifts and fast time-varying fading, severely impairing signal synchronization. Accurate Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO) estimation is critical for receiver synchronization. Nevertheless, conventional estimators and deep learning approaches often degrade significantly under highly dynamic, low-SNR conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Convolution Augmented Transformer architecture for robust, blind CFO estimation in LEO communication systems. Initially, to overcome the inherent limitations of standard linear embedding layers in capturing nonlinear phase rotations, we construct a multi-domain input feature that encompasses in-phase/quadrature (I/Q), polar, and statistical autocorrelation properties. Subsequently, a Convolutional Pre-Denoising (CPD) module, integrating multi-scale dilated convolutions and an attention mechanism, is deployed at the front end to adaptively suppress localized noise and extract robust spatiotemporal representations. These refined latent features are then processed by a Transformer encoder to explicitly track global, long-range phase dependencies. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed data-driven approach significantly outperforms conventional estimation algorithms, achieving enhanced estimation accuracy and superior resilience in highly dynamic LEO environments.

papers.title: EEGSync: Unitary Temporal Alignment Method for Naturalistic and Resting-State EEG
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) studies increasingly use naturalistic and resting-state paradigms that lack discrete event timing. These recordings contain structured oscillatory activity but often lack repeated stimulus onsets to define a shared time clock across trials or participants. We introduce EEGSync, a complex-valued unitary Procrustes temporal alignment method for band-limited analytic EEG signals. EEGSync represents each subject as a matrix of complex oscillatory trajectories and solves a unitary Procrustes problem, mapping a target subject into the temporal coordinate system of a reference or group template. The method is computationally tractable through an economy-SVD factorization that avoids constructing the full temporal operator. This alignment strictly preserves original pairwise relationships and power across EEG channels. The unitary transformation aligns latent temporal structure rather than estimating a physical clock offset. Consequently, nonlinear instantaneous measures like phase-locking value, amplitude-envelope correlation, and phase-amplitude coupling are not guaranteed to be invariant. This framing makes EEGSync highly suitable for naturalistic shared-stimulus data, and potentially useful for resting-state data as a covariance-preserving latent manifold alignment. Evaluated via subject-independent cross-validation across physiological and clinical settings, EEGSync-based features achieved an AUROC of 0.9600 and 89.45% maximum classification accuracy in eyes-open versus eyes-closed state discrimination. For Alzheimer's disease versus healthy control classification, the highest AUROC reached 0.9272 in eyes-closed recordings, with further discrimination under eyes-open photostimulation. These findings suggest temporal alignment captures discriminative information complementing conventional spectral and statistical EEG features.

papers.title: Toward Massive MIMO HAPS Networks: Antenna Architectures and Design
papers.abstract: High-altitude platform stations (HAPS) are expected to become an important component of sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks by providing wide-area wireless connectivity through massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) technology. As the communication performance of HAPS systems is fundamentally determined by the antenna array architecture, efficient antenna design has become a critical research topic. Motivated by these considerations, this article provides a comprehensive overview of antenna array design for mMIMO-enabled HAPS systems and proposes two novel antenna architectures to improve antenna-user alignment and communication performance. Specifically, the representative applications of mMIMO-enabled HAPS are first introduced, followed by the key design requirements for HAPS antenna arrays. Representative antenna architectures are then systematically reviewed and compared under a unified simulation framework based on the 3GPP NTN channel model. Finally, several promising research directions are discussed to provide insights into the design of next-generation intelligent HAPS antenna systems.

papers.title: Towards Deep Learning-Based Linear Assignment Problem Solvers for Multi-Object Tracking
papers.abstract: This paper proposes and evaluates deep learning (DL)-based linear assignment problem (LAP) solvers as a replacement for the classical Hungarian algorithm in multi-object tracking (MOT) systems. Three representative neural models are studied, namely a convolutional network (CNN), a graph neural network (GNN), and the graph-based linear assignment network (GLAN). A cost-matrix embedding is introduced so that a single model operates on cost matrices of any size, as required in MOT where the number of objects varies over time, without training a separate model for each input shape. Extensive simulations show that the embedding improves the accuracy of the neural solvers (i.e., CNN and GNN), while GLAN attains the best accuracy among them. These solvers are then integrated into a generalized labeled multi-Bernoulli (GLMB) tracker and evaluated on the WILDTRACK dataset, where GLAN yields tracking accuracy close to the Hungarian reference and comparable to recent DL-based trackers.

papers.title: Constellation Shaping for OFDM-ISAC Systems: A Systematic and Experimental Comparison
papers.abstract: Emerging integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems reuse the communications signal for radar-like sensing to provide environmental awareness. However, this integrated design imposes conflicting constraints on the modulation format, as communications systems use higher-order modulation formats while sensing systems use unit-modulus signals, making constellation shaping a key performance driver in ISAC systems. This paper develops a unified analytical and experimental framework for constellation shaping in monostatic orthogonal frequency division multiplexing ISAC systems and systematically analyzes its interaction with the three canonical sensing channel estimators (SCEs): the matched filter, the reciprocal filter, and the Wiener filter (WF). We begin by deriving constellation-dependent image signal-to-interference-and-noise ratio (ISINR) expressions for the SCEs that account for practical effects such as windowing and multi target scenarios. Based on this, we derive the corresponding entropy-maximizing channel input distributions. We generalize an autoencoder framework to optimize geometric, probabilistic, including conventional and generalized low-complexity probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS), and joint constellation shaping across all three SCEs. Extensive simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments validate the derived ISINR and show that sensing performance is governed by the SCE choice, while communications performance is dominated by the shaping method. Notably, the WF combined with joint shaping achieves the best ISAC trade-off. Low-complexity PAS variants closely approach this performance, offering a flexible trade-off and outperforming legacy modulation formats.
